section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Cutting Plane
section_1.content: Define a double cone (two cones joined at the apex) and an intersecting plane. Explain that 'Conic Sections' are the 2D shapes created when a plane slices through this 3D cone at different angles.
section_1.example: Visualize a chef slicing a carrot: the angle of the knife determines if you get a circle, ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola.

section_2.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres placed inside the cone that are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point). These points are the 'Foci' of the conic section.
section_2.example: Imagine a marble trapped inside a funnel, perfectly wedged so it touches the walls at a ring, and touched by a flat sheet of glass at one precise point.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Ellipse
section_3.content: Show a plane cutting through one nappe of the cone. Highlight two Dandelin spheres tangent to the cone above and below the plane. Explain how the sum of distances from any point on the ellipse to the two focal points (tangency points) remains constant.
section_3.example: A gardener uses two stakes and a loop of string to draw an ellipse; the Dandelin points act as those exact stakes.

section_4.title: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
section_4.content: Demonstrate what happens as the cutting plane angle changes. When parallel to the cone's edge, one sphere remains (Parabola). When cutting through both nappes, two spheres appear in separate regions (Hyperbola).
section_4.example: Use a light beam from a flashlight (cone) hitting a wall; the shape changes from a closed curve to an open, flowing curve as you tilt the light.

section_5.title: Summary and Geometric Elegance
section_5.content: Recap that Dandelin spheres provide the missing link between 3D geometric construction and 2D algebraic equations, proving that these abstract shapes are rooted in physical space.
section_5.example: A satellite dish (parabola) or a planet's orbit (ellipse)—the Dandelin spheres explain why these shapes naturally emerge in our physical universe.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Cutting Plane", [
            "Meet the double cone and the cutting plane.", 
            "Conic sections emerge from this simple intersection.", 
            "Imagine slicing a carrot at various angles.", 
            "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas are formed.", 
            "The angle determines the final geometric shape."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        plane = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.5, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/4, axis=UP).rotate(PI/6, axis=LEFT)
        
        cone_group = VGroup(cone, plane)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in a cone and a plane intersecting to form an ellipse. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        self.place_in_area(cone_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(cone_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash the plane to emphasize the intersection angle. (Color: #FF00FF)
        self.play(Flash(plane, color="#FF00FF", line_length=0.2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a normal vector to the plane to show orientation. (Color: #FFFF00)
        normal_vec = Arrow(start=plane.get_center(), end=plane.get_center() + OUT*1.5, color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(GrowArrow(normal_vec))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
